content:
Meta continues to take its artificial intelligence efforts seriously. The latest sign? A dedicated Mac app for Meta AI.

Meta joins the increasingly competitive Mac AI app market

The new Meta AI desktop app launched as a 1.0 beta and occupies just 16MB after installation.

Based on initial observation, the app is natively built for Macs running Apple Silicon and macOS 15 or later, using AppKit and SwiftUI as the shell, with WebKit rendering the richer chat experience. In other words, this is not an Electron app, nor a repackaged iPad version.

It includes Mac-specific integrations that make the desktop experience more complete than the Meta AI mobile app.

Quick Invoke uses the Option-Space keyboard shortcut to summon a slim Meta AI composition window over any working page. A separate dictation feature lets you hold a shortcut to speak and have your speech transcribed into any app, including email, documents, and even code editors.

Meta AI can also attach another Mac window to the conversation. With screen recording and accessibility permissions, the app reads the text visible in that window and takes a screenshot for your next prompt. Right now, this is a context-gathering feature, not computer control.

Beyond chat, the sidebar also includes Media, Artifacts, scheduled tasks, conversation history, and a personalization section called "About Me".

Users can switch between different thinking modes, attach files, generate media, and create recurring briefings or reminders. The app can also hide the Dock icon so it can be summoned directly through a keyboard shortcut.

Meta's recent AI deployments

The Mac app is the latest in a steady stream of new features. Back in April, Meta replaced Llama with Muse Spark. A May update added more natural voice conversation and camera-based live assistance to Meta AI.

In July, image generation powered by Muse came to Meta AI, WhatsApp, and Instagram, though Meta quickly pulled one of its features that could generate images based on public Instagram posts. Meta AI also made its way into private messaging on Threads.

Most recently, Meta rolled out Muse Code, an AI coding agent for the terminal on macOS and Linux.
